methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective cohort of 195 NUC-naive chronic HBV patients with pre-treatment serum stored between 2006-2023, median follow-up 7.4 years, and 19 incident HCC cases. Targeted lipidomics measured 158 PUFA metabolites (76 detected) via LC-MS with internal standards. PLS-DA with VIP, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction (q values), and Cox proportional hazards used. Limitations explicitly acknowledged (single center, small sample, multiple testing). However, the cut-off for 12-HHT (3.82 ng/mL) is derived from ROC on the same dataset without an independent validation cohort, risking optimism. The multivariate model with only 19 events supports at most 2 covariates by Peduzzi's rule; the model includes multiple covariates.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: HCC surveillance during NUC therapy is a real clinical need; residual HCC risk despite effective viral suppression motivates better baseline biomarkers. The combined FIB-4 + 12-HHT stratification showing 1% vs. 63% 10-year cumulative incidence is striking and clinically meaningful if validated. As a single-center retrospective cohort, LoE maps to 4.

reporting_quality.justification: Appropriate standard for a prognostic biomarker is REMARK; not explicitly cited. However, most REMARK-relevant items are present: assay platform and calibration detail, cohort definition, variable and outcome definitions, univariable and multivariable Cox HRs with 95% CIs, FDR correction, and descriptive patient characteristics in Table 1. Ethics approval numbers (1646, 3260, 4361) provided. Data and code not shared. MetaboAnalyst 6.0 platform referenced for analysis.

novelty_literature.justification: Authors plausibly claim this is the first report linking PUFA metabolites, specifically 12-HHT, with HCC development during NUC therapy. 12-HHT has been studied mainly in wound healing and intestinal barrier contexts (via BLT2); its application as an HCC predictor in HBV is novel. Biological rationale via the 12-HHT-BLT2-intestinal-barrier-microbiome-HCC axis is speculative but sensibly presented. Extends prior metabolomics reports (Gong 2017, Lu 2018) that did not include NUC therapy follow-up.

writing_presentation.justification: Manuscript is clearly written with a well-structured narrative, detailed methods, and appropriate figures. HRs and CIs are reported consistently. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings against Gong 2017 and Lu 2018 and discusses mechanistic hypotheses with appropriate hedging. Minor issues include a sentence fragment ('For whom stored serum samples collected before the initiation of therapy were available were included') and some dense passages about metabolomics methodology.

key_strengths: Long median follow-up (7.4 years) enabling 5- and 10-year HCC incidence estimates during NUC therapy, with 19 incident events
Rigorous targeted LC-MS lipidomics with deuterated internal standards (PGE2-d4, LTB4-d4, AA-d8) and 12-HHT-specific calibration curve
Multi-variable Cox modeling combined with FDR correction (q=0.013 for 12-HHT) across 14 candidate metabolites; PLS-DA used to integrate multivariate structure
Clinically meaningful combined stratification by FIB-4 and 12-HHT: 10-year cumulative HCC incidence of 1% (low/high) vs. 63% (high/low)
Plausible mechanistic framework via 12-HHT-BLT2 axis and intestinal barrier/gut microbiome connections to HCC
key_concerns: Single-center Japanese cohort (85.6% HBV genotype C) limits external generalizability; no independent validation cohort
Only 19 HCC events makes the multivariate Cox model potentially overfit relative to Peduzzi's 10-events-per-variable rule
12-HHT cutoff (3.82 ng/mL) and FIB-4 cutoff (4.08) derived from ROC on the same dataset, introducing optimism
No data or code sharing; no independent validation planned
Mechanistic hypothesis (12-HHT -> intestinal barrier -> HCC) is speculative and not experimentally tested in this work
Small subgroup counts in combined FIB-4/12-HHT strata (n=21 with both adverse markers) widen CIs considerably
chief_reviewer.rationale: Novel single-center biomarker discovery with rigorous lipidomics and appropriate statistical caveats, weakened by absence of external validation and limited events; suitable for Tier 3 specialty hepatology journal with minor revisions.
